kept.row: Hooks in the `hooks` key of settings files (2026-11-15)
kept.title: Hook `if` field stops hooks on non-tool events
kept.changed: Hook handlers in the `hooks` key of settings can carry an `if` field that only works on tool events; on other events the hook does not run.
kept.user_gets: The user sees a hook listed for an event such as SessionStart or Stop and believes it runs, while the client skips it because of the `if` field.
kept.why: hook_items in base.py makes an item for every event group in settings['hooks'] and never inspects the handlers' `if` field or the event type. A hook the client now refuses to run is still shown as active.
kept.fix: In hook_items in src/kitden/clients/base.py, check each handler in the group; when it has `if` and the event is not one of the five tool events, mark the item as not running (off) or leave it out.

kept.row: These commands work with no account: `claude --version`, `claude mcp add-json`, `get`, `list` and `remove`, `claude plugin validate --strict`, `marketplace add` and `remove`, `install`, `list --json`, `disable`, `enable` and `uninstall`; seen on Linux (2026-11-15, version 2.1.325). kept.title: Claude Code plugin install refused without a TTY for command-source plugins
kept.changed: For plugins with command-source or headersHelper entries, install without a TTY is refused with exit 1 unless -y or --accept-command is given, so the no-account install command may behave differently.
kept.user_gets: Kitden's install step for such a plugin may fail with an error in a non-TTY run, and the row's claim that install works with no account is no longer fully true; nothing wrong is shown.

kept.fix: In the contract-test row, note that install of plugins with command-source or headersHelper entries is refused without a TTY unless -y or --accept-command is given; optionally update the comment in `plugin_install_step` in `src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py`.

kept.why: plugin_remove_step uses the same flags (-s, --keep-data, --json) and the same settings key as before, so the command still works. Only the comment about the failure behaviour is now less precise (it omits the failureCode settings_still_on and the v2.1.282 requirement).
